### `payments`

[Payment Record] - This implements the recording of all monetary operations from the requirements analysis, specifically the 'secure, traceable, and compliant payment operations' and 'transaction integrity' points under AI-Driven Discount & Payment Systems. 

Maintains 3NF by separating atomic payment data from aggregated/AI-inferred outcomes. For example, each payment event (checkout, refund, wallet top-up) is represented as a unique entry, providing a clear evidence trail.

Key relationships: payment_methods for source, transactions as the business event driver, user linkage for payer/payee integrity. 
Special behaviors: immutable record post-creation (all changes are audited by payment_audit), PCI compliance enforced by business logic.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each payment record.
- `transaction_id`: Linked transaction's [transactions.id](#transactions). Connects the payment to its parent business event for traceability and reconciliation.
- `payment_method_id`: Payment method's [payment_methods.id](#payment_methods). Specifies the method used for this payment (credit card, wallet, etc).
- `amount`: [Monetary amount] - Implements the requirement for accurate financial ledger. The value of this payment, always positive. Maintains atomicity for compliance and analytics. For example, a purchase worth $99.99 or partial refund of $10.00.
- `currency`: [Currency code] - Implements multi-currency/locale requirement. 3-letter ISO code, e.g., USD, KRW, EUR. Normalized to prevent code confusion. Used for all reporting and conversions.
- `status`: [Payment status] - Implements lifecycle & auditability requirement. Values: pending, completed, failed, refunded, held, etc. Atomic by being tracked per payment; end-to-end state traces go to payment_audit table.
- `initiated_at`: [Initiation timestamp] - Implements evidence preservation and audit trail. The moment this payment operation (attempt) was started. Always set at record creation. Used for forensic traceability.
- `completed_at`: [Completion timestamp] - For state transition/tracking requirement. The moment the payment succeeded/failed. Nullable when pending. Used in compliance/reconciliation.
- `description`: [Optional payment description] - Business-facing note or payment memo. Implements requirement for evidence context/supporting documentation; not mandatory for atomicity.

### `payment_methods`

[Payment Method Catalog] - Implements the requirement for modular payment method extensibility in the Payment System Architecture section. Manages all user-supported and 3rd-party payment instruments.

Maintains 3NF by storing atomic payment instrument data for each logical method (e.g., credit card, wallet, crypto account), avoiding redundancy and storing no aggregated fields. For example, a user might have multiple cards and wallets associated here.

Key relationships: Used by payments, referenced by vouchers or campaigns. Special behaviors: supports inactivation rather than deletion for evidence preservation and ongoing compliance.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for the payment method.
- `user_id`: Belonged user's [users.id](#users). Which user owns or registers this payment method.
- `type`: [Payment method type] - Required for payment routing and compliance logic. E.g., VISA, Mastercard, PayPal, Internal Wallet, Crypto. Normalized to keep atomic per-method information. For example, prevents inconsistent labels.
- `masked_detail`: [Masked display field] - Implements PCI compliance and business UI logic for safe display. Stores last N digits or partial ID, never sensitive data. Maintains atomicity. For example, 4242 for a VISA card, 0xAb... for wallet.
- `provider`: [Provider/source platform] - For extensible payment rails and auditability. Not always present (e.g., direct bank transfer). Records vendor for reconciliation. Example: Toss, Stripe, Binance.
- `active`: [Activation flag] - Maintains audit/evidence requirements for never deleting payment methods. Only inactive if revoked/expired/deregistered. Required for evidence compliance.
- `created_at`: [Creation timestamp] - For audit trail and evidence preservation. Set on method entry record creation. Used in reporting and compliance.

### `discounts`

[Discount Record] - Implements logical representation of all discounts applied within the system, as required for 'auditable, traceable, and AI-driven discounting' in the requirements. Records only atomic logic, with all calculations performed at runtime or in materialized views.

Maintains 3NF by separating discount logic/ref into discount_rules. Applied discounts per order or item reference this table, never storing totalled values except via linkage.

Key relationships: discount_rules, orders; special behaviors: immutable after application, with all changes logged via payment_audit.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique discount operation.
- `discount_rule_id`: Linked rule's [discount_rules.id](#discount_rules). The rule which provides the logic for this discount entry.
- `order_id`: Target order's [order.id](#order). The order benefiting from this discount.
- `amount`: [Discount value] - Implements the requirement for capturing exact benefit conferred, with atomic record of the numerical value (always negative or 0). Maintains normalization and enables reconciliation/audit. For example, -5.00 for a $5 discount.
- `applied_at`: [Time of application] - Required for audit/evidence, records when the discount was actually attached to the order.
- `notes`: [Discount notes/context] - Implements requirement for transparency and traceability, e.g. which campaign, customer, or business rule applied. Atomic, optional.

### `discount_rules`

[Discount Rule Registry] - Implements modular management of discount logic for the Discount & Payment Core. Records normalized, AI/model-driven or administrator-created discount strategies, never the calculated results. Fulfills the requirement to maintain audit-ready, explainable, and reusable discount rule definitions.

3NF maintained by isolating parameters, such as type, amount, configuration, and referencing origin (e.g., campaign, voucher).

Key relationships: discount_campaigns as creators/assigners. Used by discounts. Special: deactivation for audit purposes; can reference AI model versions if used for A/B or ML-discounting.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for the discount rule.
- `campaign_id`: Discount campaign's [discount_campaigns.id](#discount_campaigns). The campaign associated with this rule for aggregation and analytics.
- `type`: [Rule type] - Required for runtime discounting. Configurable value (e.g., 'percentage', 'fixed', 'bogo', 'ml-model', etc). Enforces rule-driven modularity. Example: 'percentage' or 'dynamic-ai'.
- `value`: [Rule value] - Stores the core numeric for the discount computation (e.g., 20.0 for a 20% rule, 10.00 for $10 fixed). Maintains 3NF.
- `active`: [Activation flag] - If false, this rule is archived/disabled but included for evidence. Implements requirement for rule lifecycles and traceable config change.
- `created_at`: [Creation timestamp] - Maintains audit and compliance. For example, date when administrator or AI model created this rule.
- `ai_model_version_id`: [AI Model Version] - Links to [ai_model_versions.id](#ai_model_versions) if this rule is generated or managed by a specific AI/ML model version (for explainability, audit).

### `discount_campaigns`

[Discount Campaign Definition] - Implements requirements for campaign lifecycle, auditability, modular campaign-based discounting. Design allows grouping/analytics over a series of discounts and their rules.

Maintains full normalization by separating campaign attributes (name, time, status) from rule application.

Key relationships: discount_rules (rules), referenced from discounts/carts/orders. Special: can be deactivated but never deleted, and includes event evidence for traceability.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique discount campaign.
- `name`: [Campaign name] - Req. for grouping and operator reporting (e.g. Black Friday 2025). Atomic and normalized.
- `description`: [Campaign description] - Optional context and business notes (e.g. rules, partners). Maintains auditability.
- `start_at`: [Start time] - Implements evidence/traceability. When this campaign becomes active for discount rule matching. Maintains normalization.
- `end_at`: [End time] - Campaign end date for reporting and eligibility. Used in audits and regulatory logs. Nullable for open campaigns.
- `active`: [Campaign active flag] - If false, campaign is archived and no longer matchable. Maintains evidence, 3NF, and compliance.
- `created_at`: [Campaign creation timestamp] - Required for audit trail, reporting, and evidence. Set at insertion, not updated.

### `transactions`

[Transaction Master Record] - Fulfills the requirement that every business event causing a payment has a single, evidence-preserving, auditable record. Maintains 3NF by holding one row per transaction event (e.g. an order checkout, a wallet top-up) and separating linked payments, refunds, and discounts into their own tables.

Key relationships: Reference to orders, user. Special behaviors: immutable once recorded except notes (audited by payment_audit table), all monetary activity references a transaction id.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Represents the unique identifier for each transaction event.
- `user_id`: Transaction initiator's [users.id](#users). Links actions to specific identity for audit, fraud prevention, and analytics.
- `order_id`: Linked order's [order.id](#order). Which order or business event this transaction is for (or null for wallet loads, standalone events).
- `type`: [Transaction type] - Required, fulfills compliance for event classification (e.g. purchase, refund, credit, debit, wallet-topup). Enforces analytics/audit requirements.
- `created_at`: [Event time] - Start time of the business event, fulfills evidence requirements and enables chronological reconstruction.
- `description`: [Business event memo/description] - Optional context for reporting, audit, or customer support.

### `vouchers`

[Voucher/Loyalty Asset] - Implements the requirement for voucher, gift card, or pre-purchased credit support. Each is tracked as an independent asset, enabling compliance with prepaid, gift, refund, or promotional voucher flows.

Maintains atomic record per voucher, with lifecycle tracking for issuance, redemption, audit trail on all changes. Never deleted for evidence.

Key relationships: users (owner), payment_methods (if method-specific/voucher activation/restriction applies), campaign (for analytics/tracking), orders (redemption). Special: evidence chain for regulatory compliance.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique voucher asset.
- `user_id`: Voucher owner's [users.id](#users). For gift/asset transfer or loyalty programs.
- `campaign_id`: Issuing campaign's [discount_campaigns.id](#discount_campaigns). For business tracking and analytics integration.
- `payment_method_id`: Payment method constraint's [payment_methods.id](#payment_methods) (optional). Restricts redemption to method (e.g. in-app, crypto, external card).
- `code`: [Voucher code] - Unique, human-readable alphanumeric. Implements redemption security and audit; not a calculated field. For example: GIFT-2024-JANE-XYZ.
- `balance`: [Current amount] - The exact value (at issue or updated on use) remaining on this voucher. Edited only through auditable operations. Maintains 3NF. Example: 50.00 for $50 voucher.
- `currency`: [Voucher currency] - 3-letter ISO code; enforces multicurrency design and compliance. E.g., USD, EUR.
- `expires_at`: [Expiration date] - Timestamp when voucher becomes invalid. Nullable for non-expiring. Satisfies compliance for customer comms and refunds.
- `created_at`: [Asset issue timestamp] - When voucher assigned or loaded. Enforced as immutable. Maintains audit.
- `redeemed_at`: [Redemption/usage timestamp] - If voucher is single-use or depleted. Nullable for as-yet-unredeemed codes. Maintains normalization.

### `loyalty_points`

[Loyalty Points Ledger] - Implements loyalty programs per requirements, ensuring all point accruals/deductions are atomic, traceable, and normalized. Directly supports point-of-sale, campaign, and retroactive benefit application via reference to user/event/campaign.

Maintains one record per transaction/event (3NF), while summaries and analytics are computed in materialized views only.

Key relationships: users (owner), transactions (origin event), campaigns (linked context), referenced in rewards, discounts.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique loyalty points ledger entry.
- `user_id`: Points holder's [users.id](#users). Matches accrual/deduction to the beneficiary of points.
- `transaction_id`: Origin transaction's [transactions.id](#transactions). Details which business event granted/used points.
- `campaign_id`: Linked campaign's [discount_campaigns.id](#discount_campaigns), if any, for analytics. Nullable when directly earned (e.g. referral, review).
- `points`: [Points value] - Exact points earned/spent in this event. Always positive or negative, never calculated field. Example: 10.0 earned on purchase, -5.0 for redemption.
- `type`: [Points event type] - Required for analytics and business reporting. E.g., 'earn', 'redeem', 'bonus', 'expire'. Atomic and normalized.
- `created_at`: [Ledger event timestamp] - Required for evidence and compliance; tracks the atomic moment of this points event.

### `refunds`

[Refund Record] - Fulfills traceable, auditable refund flows for partial or full payments, applying to the PCI-regulated payment and order flows. Normalized to one row per refund event, with order, payment, and transaction references as applicable.

All refund calculations/aggregates are to be computed in views. 3NF maintained by only storing atomic per-operation data.

Key relationships: payments (source), transactions (business event), orders (context). Special: always documented in payment_audit for compliance and evidence.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique refund event.
- `payment_id`: Refunds original payment's [payments.id](#payments). Traceable, required for audit and compliance.
- `transaction_id`: Business event's [transactions.id](#transactions). The transaction driving this refund (for evidence chain and aggregation).
- `order_id`: Relevant order's [order.id](#order). Context for reporting, analytics, and recovery; nullable for standalone refunds. Fulfills regulatory traceability.
- `amount`: [Refund amount] - Atomic per-refund event (no aggregate). Value refunded in currency. Maintains audit and evidence, supports negative for chargebacks.
- `currency`: [Currency code] - Enforces multi-currency design; matches payment/order context. 3-letter ISO code.
- `status`: [Refund status] - Completes state machine for audit/compliance (e.g., requested, processed, rejected, completed). Always atomic; tracked for evidence.
- `requested_at`: [Request timestamp] - When refund request was filed. Atomic for evidence chain and customer service trace. Set at creation.
- `completed_at`: [Completion timestamp] - When refund finalized. Nullable for pending/cancelled. Maintains compliance and user transparency.
- `reason`: [Refund reason/notes] - For regulatory/contextual info. Documents why a refund is issued; atomic per event.

### `payment_audits`

[Payment/Discount/Transaction Audit Log] - Implements evidence chain, immutability, and compliance requirements from multiple specification points. This table tracks all changes (state, value, configuration) in payments, discounts, refunds, voucher activities, etc. No aggregated or calculated values are persisted; all logs are atomic, normalized events.

Each log entry references the affected entity (by type), time of event, actor (user/system). Provides audit, forensic, fraud mitigation and compliance trail.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique audit log entry.
- `user_id`: Actor's [users.id](#users). Who performed this audit-tracked action; user or system account. Null for automated events but trackable for regulatory trace.
- `entity_type`: [Entity type] - Implements polymorphic audit of payments, discounts, refunds, etc. Required for evidence/data tracking. For example: 'payment', 'discount', 'refund'.
- `entity_id`: [Entity ID] - Target entity's primary key. Maintains atomicity. For example: references payments.id or discounts.id.
- `action`: [Action taken] - Logical action (e.g., 'create', 'update', 'apply', 'fail', 'refund') accomplished by this audit event. Required for end-to-end evidence chain. Maintains normalization.
- `old_value`: [Previous state/value] - Optional snapshot for evidence. For example, payment status before update. Nullable for creates. Maintains normalization and evidence context.
- `new_value`: [New state/value] - Resulting value or config. Nullable for deletes.
- `timestamp`: [Audit event time] - Atomic/durable record of the precise event occurrence. Maintains 3NF, audit, and compliance requirements.

### `message_threads`

[Message Thread] - This implements the conversation thread grouping requirement from the 'Communication, Review & Sentiment Analysis' module. 

Groups together all related user-to-user or user-to-support messages into distinct threads, enabling clear organization and session-based conversation flows. Maintains 3NF by never storing derived or redundant message data—each thread keeps only identifying and stateful information. For example, a single thread can encompass multiple back-and-forth messages between a customer and support agent.

Key relationships: links to participants via foreign keys or through junction tables (future extension), referenced by messages and possibly notifications.
Special behaviors: Thread archival/deletion must preserve audit trails; never hard-delete for compliance.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `created_by_user_id`: Creator user's [users.id](#users).
- `subject`
  > [Thread subject] - Implements the requirement for thread labeling and discoverability.
  >
  > Business meaning: Subject or title for top-level navigation, search, and summarization. Ensures normalization by separating core thread data from actual messages. Example: 'Order #1342 Support'.
- `archived`: [Thread archival flag] - Implements requirement for evidence tracking and data preservation. Business meaning: Soft deletion/archival for audit purposes. Normalization: separate status flag, not affecting contained messages. Example: Thread archive action by user or admin.
- `created_at`: [Thread creation timestamp] - Implements audit/evidence requirement. Timestamp when thread was created. Normalization: atomic time, never duplicated from contained messages. Example: Show creation moment in thread list, regardless of message activity.
- `updated_at`: [Thread last modified timestamp] - Implements recency for sorting/searching. Updated when participants act on the thread (send/receive message, archive, etc.). Normalization: always atomic, never copied or calculated from child message times. Example: Sort by latest update in UI.

### `messages`

[Message] - Implements the transactional communication entity requirement from the 'Communication, Review, and Sentiment Analysis' document. 

Represents individual messages (text, image, or system notification) exchanged within a message thread. Maintains strict 3NF—only atomic message and linkage data. For example, a customer question and a vendor response, with each message linked to user and thread.

Key relationships: references sender (user), target thread, and optionally parent message (for replies/quoting). 
Special behaviors: All changes are audited; messages are never deleted, only flagged. Attachments/media handled externally for evidence integrity.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `thread_id`: Thread's [message_threads.id](#message_threads) this message belongs to.
- `sender_user_id`: Sender's [users.id](#users).
- `parent_message_id`: Optional parent message's [messages.id](#messages) for reply/tree structure.
- `content`: [Message content] - Implements the raw message body/evidence tracking. Primary user/customer or system content. Never pre-calculated. Example: Support question, reply, or notification message.
- `message_type`: [Message type] - Implements conversational workflow logic. Values include: 'user', 'system', 'notification', or custom types. Maintains normalization by storing type info atomically. Example: 'user' = human, 'system' = order status update, etc.
- `sent_at`: [Send timestamp] - Time the message was dispatched. Maintains normalization by being atomic, always set on creation. Example: Populate message log or sort.
- `read_at`: [Read timestamp] - Time the recipient viewed the message. Maintains normalization by being optional, never duplicated or inferred. Example: Unread badge logic.
- `archived`: [Archived flag] - Strict evidence preservation, marking messages without deletion. Normalization compliance: atomic per message, not inherited from thread. Example: Hide from primary inbox but retained for audit.

### `notifications`

[Notification] - Implements the user notification system requirement as described under communication/event modules. 

Captures system-/event-driven notifications linked to users and, if relevant, threads or orders. Maintains 3NF by never duplicating event data from source entities; only logs atomic notification facts. Example: 'Order shipped', 'New message', or 'Sale started'.

Key relationships: references user, may link to thread or other context entity.
Special behaviors: Tracks read/unread status and delivery timestamp; old records never deleted for evidence.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `user_id`: Notified user's [users.id](#users).
- `thread_id`: Related thread's [message_threads.id](#message_threads), if any.
- `notification_type`: [Type indicator] - Implements notification categorization; e.g., 'system', 'message', 'promotion'. Normalization: Single source of event type per notification. Example: Used for filtering in notification center.
- `content`: [Notification content] - Implements atomic event evidence; real message dispatched to user. Normalization: content held here, not duplicated from other entities. Example: 'Your order #1234 shipped'.
- `sent_at`: [Notification dispatch time] - Time when delivered to user. Normalization: atomic per notification. Example: Sorting notifications, TTL enforcement.
- `read_at`: [Notification read time] - When user viewed notification. Normalization: atomic, optional per record. Example: Mark as read upon open.
- `archived`: [Archived flag] - Keeps notification for historical evidence. Never physically deleted. Example: Mute or archive by user action.

### `reviews`

[Review] - Implements product/service review entity from the 'Communication, Review & Sentiment Analysis' business module.

Represents authentic and versioned user-submitted reviews. Maintains strict 3NF: only atomic review attributes—content, media, metadata, never derived or aggregated. Example: User review for a purchased product, versioned for edit history.

Key relationships: References user, product/service, ties to moderation and sentiment logs.
Special behaviors: Supports multilingual data, evidence archiving, evidence-preserving versioning for edits and compliance.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `user_id`: Author user's [users.id](#users).
- `product_id`: Reviewed product's [products.id](#products).
- `parent_review_id`: Optional parent review's [reviews.id](#reviews), for reply/hierarchical structure.
- `content`: [Review content] - Main review body, implements the core business requirement for evidence-preserved user feedback. Normalization: only atomic text here. Example: User's product experience.
- `language_code`: [Review language code] - Implements multicultural and accessibility requirement. Holds locale for review. Normalization: only atomic value, never derived. Example: 'en', 'ko', 'fr'.
- `created_at`: [Review creation timestamp] - When submitted by user. Example: timeline displays, compliance logs.
- `updated_at`: [Last modification time] - Latest edit, present on update. Example: show edit history.
- `verified_purchase`: [Purchase verification flag] - Implements fraud prevention and authenticity. Set if review relates to verified purchase. Example: 'True' for eligible buyers only.
- `archived`: [Archived flag] - Soft delete for audit and evidence. Never physically removed. Example: Admin-moderated reviews.

### `review_media`

[Review Media] - Implements the requirement to allow image/video attachments for reviews while enforcing normalization and evidence archiving.

References review, media asset, and stores metadata. Only atomic linkage and media attributes; evaluation or calculated fields in other tables only (e.g., media count in views). Example: Multiple images for a product review.

Key relationships: references review and an external media entity (for expansion). 
Special behaviors: Only links and descriptive attributes; media storage handled elsewhere.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `review_id`: Linked review's [reviews.id](#reviews).
- `media_type`: [Attachment type] - 'image', 'video', etc. Normalization: atomic classification. Example: Used for gallery, filter.
- `uri`: [Media URI] - Directly links to storage asset. Maintains normalization by not duplicating data. Example: S3/GCS location or CDN path.
- `alt_text`: [Alt text] - Accessibility and multicultural support. Describes image/video for a11y. Example: 'User photo of red sneakers'.
- `sequence`: [Display sequence] - Implements ordered media logic. Maintains normalized integer, not inferred or derived. Example: Order of images as shown in UI.

### `review_moderations`

[Review Moderation] - Implements evidence-preserved moderation actions on reviews as required by compliance, fraud prevention, and audit modules. 

Stores atomic records of each moderation: action, moderator, decision, timestamp, rationale. Maintains strict normalization (no aggregation, no calculated fields). Example: Admin removes, restores, or flags a review for abusive content.

Key relationships: references moderated review and moderator user.
Special behaviors: All moderation events strictly immutable, producing an audit trail.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `review_id`: Moderated review's [reviews.id](#reviews).
- `moderator_user_id`: Moderator user's [users.id](#users).
- `action_type`: [Moderation action] - 'remove', 'restore', 'flag', etc. Required for audit. Example: Used as evidence on compliance review.
- `rationale`: [Reason/rationale] - Explanation by moderator. Normalization: only atomic string. Example: Why review was removed/flagged.
- `created_at`: [Timestamp] - When moderation occurred. Normalized as atomic point in time. Example: Legal holds.

### `review_sentiments`

[Review Sentiment] - Implements versioned and AI-powered sentiment analysis for reviews as described in Sentiment Analysis requirements.

Captures analysis model/version, result, and timestamp for every processed review. Maintains strict normalization: no pre-calculated fields. Example: 'Positive/negative/neutral' per review version, tied to model run.

Key relationships: references review and AI model/version.
Special behaviors: Multiple entries allowed for model runs, with timestamped trail for evidence.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `review_id`: Analyzed review's [reviews.id](#reviews).
- `ai_model_version_id`: AI model version's [ai_model_versions.id](#ai_model_versions) used for analysis.
- `sentiment`: [Sentiment result] - Implements the core outcome (e.g., 'positive', 'negative', 'neutral'). Atomic per analysis, never derived. Example: For dashboard reporting.
- `score`: [Sentiment score] - Numeric value indicating polarity/confidence. Maintains normalization as atomic output. Example: Model's confidence in prediction.
- `analyzed_at`: [Timestamp] - When sentiment analysis executed.

### `sentiment_analysis_logs`

[Sentiment Analysis Log] - Implements full evidence and model input/output preservation for every sentiment analysis run, fulfilling the tracking requirements set in advanced AI and compliance modules.

Stores all model input, output, AI version, and raw evidence for legal hold/audit. Maintains strict 3NF by holding only atomic data elements, never calculated or aggregate. Example: A record per sentiment inference, with trace of data and rationale.

Key relationships: references review, ai_model_version.
Special behaviors: Immutable, long-retained for compliance and model debugging.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `review_id`: Analyzed review's [reviews.id](#reviews).
- `ai_model_version_id`: AI version's [ai_model_versions.id](#ai_model_versions) used for sentiment.
- `raw_input`: [Raw model input] - Stores original text or preprocessed structure input to model. Maintains normalization: atomic capture only. Example: JSON of features or string blob.
- `output`: [Raw model output] - Full inference result, possibly JSON. Maintains normalization, not aggregated. Example: Model's output structure as-is for trace/debug.
- `model_version`: [Model version string] - Redundant to FK for compliance readability. Maintains normalization: atomic version string. Example: 'v1.2.2-EN-SENTIMENT'.
- `analyzed_at`: [Analysis timestamp] - When analysis was run. Maintains normalization as atomic timestamp. Example: Compliance audit.

### `favorites`

[Favorites Management Table] - This implements the favorite/bookmarking system as specified in section 07 of the requirements report.

Manages the user's bookmarks and favorite items, supporting evidence-based, auditable user preference tracking. Maintains 3NF by separating only the favorite relationship (user-content), leaving additional data (history, metadata, personalization) in related entities. For example, this table allows users to mark any product as a favorite and organizes the link between user and product for AI/analytics workflows.

Key relationships: Linked to [users.id](#users), [products.id](#products), with cascaded deletion on user or product removal.
Special behaviors: Immutable, evidence-preserving (soft-delete with audit via personalization_audit), composite uniqueness constraint to ensure a user cannot favorite the same product twice.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique favorite record identifier, complying with audit and evidence requirements.
- `user_id`
  > Belonged user's [users.id](#users).
  > Links the favorite action to the profile, supporting analytics, consent, and privacy compliance.
- `product_id`
  > Target product's [products.id](#products).
  > Points to the favorited product, supporting contextual personalization, product analytics, and AI recommendations.
- `created_at`: Timestamp for when the favorite record was created. Implements evidence preservation and auditing as required in the compliance sections. For example, enables reconstructing user preference timelines.
- `deleted_at`: Soft-deletion timestamp to maintain evidence preservation and non-repudiation. Null if active. For example, keeps an audit trail for regulatory requests.

### `bookmarks`

[Bookmark Table] - Implements user-defined bookmark/organization of products/content, as called for in the Favorites and Personalization requirements.

Acts as a refinement on the favorite concept, enabling organization and metadata for bookmarks. Maintains normalization (3NF) by linking only user and product, and keeping additional metadata (e.g. category/folder/tag) here, rather than the core favorite link. For example, a user can tag or categorize favorites using bookmarks.

Key relationships: Linked to [users.id](#users) and [products.id](#products); supports bidirectional linkage for advanced queries and analytics.
Special behaviors: Composite uniqueness constraint for per-user bookmarks; supports optional custom_folder for personalized organization.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique bookmark identifier.
- `user_id`
  > Belonged user's [users.id](#users).
  > Supports permission checks, analytics, and data retrieval.
- `product_id`
  > Referenced product's [products.id](#products).
  > Pinpoints the bookmarked product for analysis and retrieval.
- `custom_folder`: Optional organizational label or folder for this bookmark. Implements user segmentation for evidence and personalization. For example, user groups bookmarks under "Wish List".
- `tag`: Optional user-defined tag for the bookmark for enhanced organization and analytics. Maintains normalization and is kept atomic. For example: "Winter Sale".
- `note`: Optional user note attached to the bookmark, evidence for personalization. For example, "Gift idea for Mom."
- `created_at`: Timestamp for bookmark creation, audit and personalization evidence compliance.
- `deleted_at`: Optional timestamp for soft deletion (audit/evidence preservation requirement).

### `personalization_events`

[Personalization Event Table] - Implements tracking of all personalization actions/events impacting user experience, specified in section 07 and 08 (AI & Data Operations).

Captures evidence and metadata for when a user receives, reacts to, or interacts with a personalized recommendation. Maintains 3NF by relegating feature data and detailed analytics logs to other tables. For example, this enables tracing which recommendation was shown, clicked, or dismissed.

Key relationships: Linked to [users.id](#users), [recommendations.id](#recommendations), [products.id](#products). Supports AI model tracking.
Special behaviors: Immutable event log for audit/compliance, supports detailed event-type taxonomy via 'event_type'.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique record for a personalization event.
- `user_id`: Belonged user's [users.id](#users). Links event to user profile for analytics and personalization history.
- `recommendation_id`: Belonged recommendation's [recommendations.id](#recommendations). Reference to the suggestion served in this event.
- `product_id`: Target product's [products.id](#products). The product associated with the event, for traceability and feedback learning.
- `event_type`: Type of personalization event (e.g., view, click, save, dismiss). Enables advanced analytics and model explainability. Normalized—categorical and atomic. For example: 'RECOMMENDATION_SERVED'.
- `model_version`: AI/ML model version used in generating the recommendation; implements explainability and regulatory compliance requirements.
- `context`: Optional context information for event (device, locale, etc.). Captures multi-channel/locale evidence as per requirements.
- `timestamp`: Timestamp for when personalization event occurred. Implements evidence and audit traceability.

### `recommendations`

[Recommendation Table] - Implements the storage of AI/ML-driven recommendation deliveries as required for personalization, evidence tracking, and explainability (requirements sections 07 & 08).

Each record links a recommendation to a user and a product at a specific time, tracks which model/version served it, and whether the result was seen or acted upon. Maintains normalization by not pre-calculating favorites or analytics.

Key relationships: References [users.id](#users) (who received), [products.id](#products) (recommended content), and links to personalization events.
Special behaviors: Composite uniqueness for user, product, and timestamp (cannot re-recommend exact same thing at the same time), GIN index for rationale explainability/search.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique recommendation record.
- `user_id`: Belonged user's [users.id](#users). User receiving the recommendation.
- `product_id`: Target product's [products.id](#products). Product being recommended.
- `model_id`: AI model identifier generating the recommendation; for compliance and retrain audit.
- `model_version`: AI/ML model version generating this recommendation. Required for audit and transparency (regulatory).
- `rationale`: Optional human/machine-readable rationale, used for explainability and audit trail per compliance needs.
- `recommendation_time`: Timestamp when recommendation was delivered. Required for continuous feedback/monitoring.

### `personalization_audits`

[Personalization Audit Table] - Implements the evidence-preserving audit log for all personalization and favorite-related actions, as required for regulatory, explainability, and continuous improvement needs (sections 07, 08, 09). 

Stores non-repudiable, immutable evidence for sensitive user actions related to favorites, bookmarks, recommendations, and AI-triggered changes. Maintains full normalization by referencing all participating entities and ensuring no pre-calculated or derived fields.

Key relationships: References [users.id](#users), [favorites.id](#favorites), [bookmarks.id](#bookmarks), [recommendations.id](#recommendations), [personalization_events.id](#personalization_events). Cross-links actions for holistic compliance and model improvement.
Special behaviors: Write-once (append-only), cryptographically signed evidence, all fields atomic.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique audit record.
- `user_id`: Belonged user's [users.id](#users). Links the personalization action to specific user.
- `favorite_id`: Optional reference to [favorites.id](#favorites), maintained for evidence and retroactive compliance.
- `bookmark_id`: Optional reference to [bookmarks.id](#bookmarks), maintained for evidence and retroactive compliance.
- `recommendation_id`: Optional reference to [recommendations.id](#recommendations), to track audit events involving recommendations.
- `personalization_event_id`: Optional link to [personalization_events.id](#personalization_events), audit evidence for anything with contextual event.
- `action_type`: Type/category of the audit event (e.g. ADD_FAVORITE, REMOVE_BOOKMARK, SERVE_RECOMMENDATION). Normalized/atomic for querying/compliance. For example: 'ACTIONS'.
- `evidence_hash`: Cryptographic hash of the action/event for non-repudiation, as required for compliance.
- `timestamp`: Exact time of audit event for regulatory trace/compliance; enables reconstructing chain-of-custody.

### `ai_models`

AI Model Registry - This implements the requirement for a unified model registry and governance from section 08 (Advanced AI and Data Operations) of the requirements. 

Central repository for all AI/ML models used within the system, holding business metadata (name, description, model type, owner), categorization, and audit fields to enforce model governance, version tracking, and compliance. Maintains 3NF by not duplicating version, deployment, or decision info. For example, registering recommendation, dynamic pricing, or sentiment models. 

Key relationships: Connects with [ai_model_versions](#ai_model_versions) for actual model instances, links to organizations and users for ownership, supports audit evidence. 
Special behaviors: Uniqueness constraint on (name, organization), all business fields are atomic and normalized.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key - Unique identifier for each AI model.
- `organization_id`: Owning organization's [organizations.id](#organizations) - Implements multidomain model governance requirement. Organization context for model accountability.
- `owner_id`: Owning user's [users.id](#users) - Maintains audit trace and role-based model management.
- `name`: Model name - Implements model identification aspect. Human-friendly, unique per organization. Prevents duplication, maintains normalization. Example: 'prod-recommendation-2024'
- `model_type`: Model type - Implements model taxonomy. Business meaning: e.g., recommendation, pricing, fraud. Ensures model classification is atomic. Example: 'recommendation'
- `description`: Description - Human-intelligible summary, implements evidence/traceability requirement. For example: 'Collaborative filtering model for top sellers'.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp - When model metadata was first registered. Atomic, not derived.
- `updated_at`: Update timestamp - When model metadata was last changed. Ensures normalization. Example: model taxonomy change.

### `ai_model_versions`

AI Model Versioning - Implements the requirement for full model lifecycle tracking and explainability from section 08 (Advanced AI and Data Operations) requirement.

Stores concrete versioned instances for each AI model, supporting lineage and deployment traceability. Complies with 3NF by never embedding decision or request data, only atomic version metadata. For example, each trained model artifact, versioned and ready for deployment or audit. 

Key relationships: Foreign key to [ai_models](#ai_models), holds deployment metadata. Special behaviors: Unique constraint on (ai_model_id, version_hash).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key - Unique identifier for each model version.
- `ai_model_id`: Parent model's [ai_models.id](#ai_models) - Traces version lineage. Enforces normalization: no model metadata duplication.
- `version`: Version string - Implements versioning policy. e.g., 'v1.4.3', ensures atomicity, never derived. For tracking deployments.
- `version_hash`: Version hash - Immutable hash of model artifact, supporting evidence preservation and integrity verification. For compliance (e.g. audit trails).
- `artifact_url`: Artifact URI - Location of the model artifact in secure storage. Ensures normalization by referencing only, not storing contents.
- `framework`: ML framework - Business context: e.g., 'TensorFlow', 'PyTorch'. Maintains atomic, normalized record of build platform.
- `metadata`: Version metadata - Implements evidence trace. JSON or key-value string for atomic version-specific fields (hyperparameters, notes). Never derived.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp - Atomic, when this version was created.
- `deployed_at`: Deployment timestamp - When this model version was deployed (if ever). Null if never deployed. Atomic. For regulatory/audit evidence.

### `ai_training_data`

AI Training Data Registry - Implements mandatory dataset tracking requirement from Advanced AI and Data Operations section.

Catalogs all datasets—internal or external—used in AI/ML training runs. Business purpose: ensuring evidence preservation, model governance, and regulatory compliance. 3NF maintained: no embedding feature or decision data, only atomic dataset metadata. For example, registering user purchase logs, product metadata, reviews, or imported partners' data feeds as AI input.

Key relationships: Models dataset-to-model and version relationships, supports traceability. Special behaviors: Uniqueness constraint on (name, version, source_uri).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key - Unique identifier for training dataset.
- `ai_model_id`: Associated model's [ai_models.id](#ai_models) - Optional, as datasets may predate or span multiple models. Maintains traceable, normalized context.
- `name`: Dataset name - Human-friendly identifier, e.g., '2024Q1-purchases'. Required. Normalization via uniqueness constraint with version+uri.
- `version`: Dataset version - e.g., 'v1', '202404', for traceability and reproducibility. Implements evidence requirement. Required.
- `source_uri`: Source URI - Link to immutable, secured dataset in storage. Ensures data separation, not duplication. Required.
- `schema_hash`: Schema hash - Hash of dataset schema, for evidence and change detection. Ensures atomicity, never derived.
- `record_count`: Record count - Number of records/rows in the dataset. Atomic, reported only. Example: 10000000 (for 10M sale records).
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp - When dataset was first registered.

### `ai_feature_store`

AI Feature Store Registry - Implements the centralized feature tracking and evidence preservation requirement from the Advanced AI and Data Operations section.

Native registry for feature sets engineered for AI model training and inference. 3NF is ensured: field-level definitions of each feature set, no denormalization or pre-calculation. For example, storing user-product interaction feature set names, their schema description, and originating training dataset.

Key relationships: Links to [ai_training_data](#ai_training_data) (origin of features) and [ai_model_versions](#ai_model_versions) (using version). Special behaviors: Uniqueness constraint on (ai_model_version_id, name).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key - Unique identifier for a feature set.
- `ai_model_version_id`: Target model version's [ai_model_versions.id](#ai_model_versions) - Implements model lineage traceability requirement. Required.
- `ai_training_data_id`: Source dataset's [ai_training_data.id](#ai_training_data) - Evidence link for feature extraction. Nullable, not all features require direct linkage. Maintains normalization.
- `name`: Feature set name - Human-friendly label, e.g. 'user-purchase-matrix-v1'. Normalized and unique per model version. Example: 'sentiment-review-set-202404'.
- `description`: Description - Detailed documentation for audit/compliance. Evidence trace for explainability. Example: 'Features for collaborative filtering.'
- `schema`: Feature schema - Machine-readable JSON schema representing the feature set structure. Maintains normalization; no denormalized data here.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp - Evidence of when engineering completed.

### `ai_decision_logs`

AI Decision Log - Implements mandatory logging and explainability requirement from Advanced AI and Data Operations section.

Immutable, atomic record of each automated decision or inference by any AI model. Business purpose: evidence for compliance (GDPR 'right to explanation'), debugging, monitoring, and model improvement. Keeps schema atomic: never stores denormalized or summarized results, only per-decision facts and links. For example, logging a recommendation output for a specific user or order.

Key relationships: References [ai_model_version](#ai_model_version), target entity (user, product, order, etc.), audit details. Special behaviors: Enforces data provenance via foreign keys and immutable timestamps.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key - Unique identifier for a decision log.
- `ai_model_version_id`: Associated model version's [ai_model_versions.id](#ai_model_versions) - Tracks which version produced this decision. Required.
- `target_user_id`: Target user's [users.id](#users) - The user affected by decision. Nullable where not user-specific. Maintains normalization, never derived.
- `target_entity`: Target entity - Implements audit tracking of affected object. E.g., 'order', 'product', 'review'. Prevents denormalization by not embedding entity fields.
- `target_entity_id`: Target entity ID - The ID of the affected object (atomic, never joined/duplicated), e.g. product or order ID. Maintains strict normalization.
- `decision`: Decision outcome - E.g., 'recommend', 'block', 'price=12.50'. Business context: ensures traceability, atomicity, never computed. For model explainability.
- `input_snapshot`: Input snapshot - JSON or base64 blob representing the exact input to the AI at inference, for audit and debugging. 3NF: atomic per event.
- `rationale`: Model rationale - Explanation for the decision, if available. Supports compliance, 3NF, and human override/audit.
- `created_at`: Timestamp of decision event for audit/evidence.

### `ai_feedback`

AI Feedback Log - Implements feedback loop requirement for continuous learning and audit from Advanced AI and Data Operations section.

Stores explicit and implicit feedback for each AI decision event, connecting user actions or operator overrides to the original model inference. Enables automated model retraining, human override validation, and explainability for regulators. 3NF strict: each field atomic, all links explicit, no denormalization.

Key relationships: Links [ai_decision_logs](#ai_decision_logs) (original decision), user, and model version. Special behaviors: Composite index on (decision_log_id, user_id, feedback_type).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key - Unique identifier for feedback event.
- `decision_log_id`: Original decision log's [ai_decision_logs.id](#ai_decision_logs) - Implements feedback-data linkage for model retraining. Required.
- `user_id`: User's [users.id](#users) submitting feedback or being observed for implicit signals. Allows anonymous/null for auto signals.
- `feedback_type`: Type of feedback - E.g., 'accepted', 'dismissed', 'overridden', 'implicit-click'. Atomic per event. Implements feedback/data tracking requirement.
- `feedback_value`: Feedback value - E.g., 'positive', 'negative', 'rating=5'. Business context: for retraining, analysis. Strictly atomic, not computed.
- `metadata`: Metadata - (Optional) JSON/string with UI context, device info, or feedback rationale. Atomic/non-derived, supports explainability.
- `created_at`: Timestamp of feedback event. Maintains evidence, not derived.

### `security_event`

Security Event Logging - This implements event logging and evidence preservation for all security-relevant actions as per Section 2 (Critical Data Auditing) and Section 4 (Data Integrity & Preservation) of the requirements. 

Records all system-level security-related occurrences, capturing actor, context, and timestamp for each. Maintains 3NF by storing only atomic event-level data and referencing origin entities via foreign keys. For example, an API token rotation, a failed login attempt, or privilege escalation. Key relationships: links to relevant user, session, and API client where applicable. Special behaviors: immutable; no deletion, supports audit retrieval.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each security event record.
- `user_id`: Reference to initiating user's [users.id](#users). If system-initiated, can be null. Ensures mapping of event context to user for audit.
- `session_id`: Associated session [sessions.id](#sessions). Links actions to active session for traceability.
- `api_client_id`: API client context [api_clients.id](#api_clients) under which the event occurred, if relevant.
- `event_type`: Category of security event (e.g., 'login_attempt', 'token_rotation', 'permission_update') - Implements Section 2 (Critical Data Auditing). Encodes nature of event for context-rich evidence. For example, used for analytics and compliance dashboards. Required.
- `event_details`: Human- and machine-readable details of the event - Implements evidence preservation requirement. Provides business context; can include affected fields, prior values, or policy triggers. For example, stores JSON stringified details. Required.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp of the event record - Ensures non-repudiation as required for audit trails and regulatory compliance.

### `permission`

Permission Registry - This implements dynamic and fine-grained permission tracking aligned to Section 3 (Access Control & Permission). 

Tracks all permissions available in the platform, with atomic records for each permission entity. 3NF maintained: only basic attributes and references to associated policy. For example, permissions like 'order.edit', 'discount.apply'. Key relationships: can be referenced in policy and role mappings. Special behaviors: unique codes enforced, never deleted (for historical policy linkage).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for permission.
- `policy_id`: Associated policy's [policy.id](#policy). Connects permission entity to rules and conditions applying to it.
- `code`: Unique permission code (e.g., 'user.read', 'order.cancel') - Implements fine-grained access control as required by Section 3. For example, used in runtime permission checks. Must be unique across system. Required.
- `description`: Detailed description of what the permission entails - Maps to regulatory and explainability requirements. For example, describes business context for UI and audit tools. Required.
- `created_at`: Timestamp of permission creation - For audit and evidence preservation as per requirements.

### `policy`

Permission Policy - This model implements Section 3 and 5 (dynamic policy-driven permission enforcement, regulatory compliance tracking). 

Represents a logical grouping of permissions with optional conditions or constraints. Maintains 3NF by storing only atomic policy-level data. For example, policies for 'admin_only', time-bound permissions, region-limited access. Key relationships: can be referenced by permissions, roles, or external API modules. Special behaviors: policies remain after deletion for legal traceability.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for a policy.
- `name`: Human-readable policy name - Implements requirement for business logic explainability and traceability. For example, 'Admin Global', 'EU Data Export'. Required.
- `conditions`: Serialized JSON or code describing policy constraints/logic - Aligns with dynamic enforcement and compliance. For example, specifies conditions such as 'only during office hours'. Required.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp for policy record - Provides evidence trail needed for audits. Required.

### `audit_log`

System Audit Log - Implements end-to-end non-repudiable logging for all system and user actions, in accordance with Section 4 and 5 (Data Integrity, Evidence, Audit-Ready Structure). 

Stores immutable audit records for every critical operation and event. 3NF achieved by isolating raw events with user, entity, and context references. Used for regulatory export, legal inquiry, and breach forensics. Key relationships: links to user, affected entity (as foreign key where possible), evidence_archive. Special behaviors: append-only; deletion prohibited.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique audit log record identifier.
- `user_id`: User actor responsible for action [users.id](#users). Enables user-centric audit filtering for compliance exports.
- `evidence_archive_id`: Archived evidence snapshot [evidence_archive.id](#evidence_archive) associated with event.
- `action`: Type of action performed (e.g., 'create', 'update', 'delete', 'payment.approve') - Implements requirement for business trace and explainability. For example, facilitates compliance dashboard queries. Required.
- `entity_type`: Type of entity affected (e.g., 'order', 'user', 'review') - Enables entity-level filtering and integrity checks. Required.
- `entity_id`: ID of the affected entity instance - Ensures traceability down to individual records, fulfilling audit trail requirements. Nullable for system events not targeting specific entity.
- `context`: JSON-encoded metadata/context of the audit event - Supports regulatory and forensics use. For example, before/after data, machine/environmental context. Required.
- `created_at`: Timestamp of audit log creation - For evidence and compliance enforcement. Required.

### `compliance_report`

Compliance Report - This table fulfills Section 5 requirements for regulatory export, oversight, and drilldown on AI-driven or security events. 

Stores generated compliance reports (GDPR, CCPA, internal regs) and their metadata. Maintains 3NF by only referencing report owner/user, storing atomic report attributes. For example, a GDPR export delivered to a user, or a monthly payment compliance summary. Key relationships: owners (user, organization), linked evidence. Special behaviors: cannot be edited once published, may be superseded by later reports.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique compliance report identifier.
- `user_id`: Owner or data subject [users.id](#users) for individual reports.
- `organization_id`: Owning organization [organizations.id](#organizations), if applicable.
- `report_type`: Classification of compliance report (e.g., 'GDPR_EXPORT', 'CCPA_AUDIT') - Implements export and oversight requirements. Required.
- `status`: Status of report (e.g., 'pending', 'published', 'superseded') - Ensures auditability of report progression. For example, status visible in admin dashboards. Required.
- `generated_at`: Timestamp when report was generated - For audit and tracking as per requirements. Required.
- `published_at`: Timestamp when report was published/delivered; required for evidence trail and deadline compliance. Nullable if not yet published.

### `data_retention`

Data Retention Policy - This implements configurable data retention, deletion, and legal hold logic (Section 5), supporting entity-level configurations and traceability.

Stores data retention policy per data subject or entity. 3NF maintained by separating atomic policy settings per record. For example, policies for user data, payment log, or review. Key relationships: can be linked to entity, organization, user for context. Special behaviors: enforced by backend logic, referenced by compliance_report, deletion must leave audit trace.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key for data_retention policy record.
- `organization_id`: Organization to which retention policy applies [organizations.id](#organizations). Enables B2B use cases and regulatory separation.
- `entity_type`: Entity data type subject to retention policy (e.g., 'user', 'order', 'review') - Aligns with regulatory entity-level retention needs. Required.
- `retention_period_days`: Retention period in days (e.g., 365, 1095) - Ensures compliance with regulatory and contract requirements. For example, controls automated deletion logic. Required.
- `is_legal_hold`: Legal hold status - Implements requirement for holding deletion in progress during litigation/audit. For example, backend logic enforces this. Required.
- `created_at`: Policy record creation time - Fulfills requirement for audit trail per policy change. Required.

### `evidence_archive`

Evidence Archive - Implements immutable, compressed archiving for critical evidence as required in Section 4 (Evidence Preservation) and Section 5 (Compliance). 

Stores compressed or signed evidence payloads for system operations, enabling legal, forensics, and audit exports. 3NF enforced by separating blob storage and atomic references. For example, a zipped export of user data provided for GDPR DSAR; a signed PDF of payment logs. Key relationships: referenced in audit_log, compliance_report, and other tables where evidence may be required. Special behaviors: blob/blob reference is immutable and append-only; cannot be deleted, only superseded.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique evidence archive record identifier.
- `evidence_type`: Type/category of archived evidence (e.g., 'GDPR_DSAR_EXPORT', 'PAYMENT_LOG_SNAPSHOT') - Fulfilling evidence preservation and compliance needs. Required.
- `blob_url`: URI for archived evidence binary/payload - Implements requirement for logical separation of data and reference. For example, S3/GCS/Blob Storage link. Required.
- `size_bytes`: Size of the archived evidence in bytes - For audit, integrity, and storage cost assessment. Fulfills traceability requirements. Required.
- `checksum`: Cryptographic hash (e.g., SHA256) for the stored evidence - Implements data integrity and non-repudiation patterns. Required.
- `created_at`: Timestamp of evidence creation/archival. Supports evidence chain enforcement. Required.

### `api_clients`

[API Client Registry] - This implements the client registration and management requirement for API and omnichannel extensibility from the scalability and integration section of the requirements. 

Business explanation: Represents all third-party, partner, or internal software clients authorized to interact with the platform via APIs or omnichannel connectors. Maintains 3NF compliance by only storing atomic client metadata and security configuration, with all usage/interaction history managed in separate audit/sessions models. For example, a registered ERP partner system or mobile app client would have an instance here.

Key relationships: Connected to API tokens (for issued secrets), audit logs (for operations), and integration channels (for channel associations).
Special behaviors: Certificate/public-key fields, client revocation and expiration, and strict uniqueness on client_name.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `client_name`
  > [Client Name] - Implements the requirement for unique human-readable identification of the API/omnichannel client.
  >
  > Used for admin UI and logging, not as technical credential. Ensures normalization by separating identity from secrets. Example: 'Acme ERP Gateway'.
- `description`
  > [Description] - Brief business description of client/app integration.
  >
  > For admins, auditability, and risk/compliance review. Atomic string for documentation. Example: 'Official mobile application for end-users.'
- `contact_email`
  > [Contact Email] - Administrative contact for support/issues.
  >
  > Used for notifications, incident response. Not a user reference. Atomic and unique per client. Example: 'devops@partner.com'.
- `public_key`
  > [Public Key or Certificate] - Implements the API client verification requirement for secure request signing, especially for B2B/integrated clients.
  >
  > Stored as text blob. No duplication or relational data. Example: PEM key/certificate.
- `is_active`
  > [Activation Status] - Is this API client currently permitted to call APIs/integrations?
  >
  > Implements the enable/disable for operational security and access controls. Not derived, not transitive. Example: Initially true upon onboarding.
- `created_at`
  > [Creation Timestamp] - When this client entry was registered.
  >
  > Evidence for audit, onboarding, and rotation policies. Atomic timestamp.
- `deleted_at`
  > [Revocation (Soft Delete) Timestamp] - When this client integration was revoked, decommissioned, or scheduled for archival.
  >
  > Evidence for audit/forensics. Soft delete pattern.

### `api_tokens`

[API Access Token] - This implements the secure API authentication/authorization requirement, tracking all issued credentials for API and integration client access, mapped to requirements for token lifecycle management and security event monitoring. 

Business explanation: Stores all tokens/secrets granted to a specific API client. Maintains 3NF: token value, issued scope, and expiry are atomic, with usage logs and audit in secondary tables. For example, an OAuth2/JWT token for Acme's integration client. 

Key relationships: Linked to api_clients, with cascaded deletion/invalidation support. 
Special behaviors: Token revocation, rotation, scope definition, expiry, and linkage to session and audit models.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `api_client_id`
  > [API Client Reference] - Belonged API client's [api_clients.id](#api_clients).
  >
  > Links the token to its registered client application for evidence and access validation.
- `token_value`
  > [Token Value] - Implements requirement to securely store issued access token (hashed/encrypted).
  >
  > Atomic (not derived), never duplicated in plain text. Example: Hashed OAuth2 JWT or custom token.
- `scope`
  > [Token Scope] - Business/technical permission associated with this token.
  >
  > Stored as delimited/structured string for 3NF. Example: 'read:orders,write:catalog'.
- `issued_at`
  > [Token Issued At] - Timestamp of when the token was created/granted.
  >
  > Strict evidence and compliance requirement.
- `expires_at`
  > [Token Expiry] - When this access credential will expire, per business security/compliance rules.
  >
  > Atomic timestamp value. For example, 7 days from issue.
- `revoked_at`
  > [Token Revocation Timestamp] - If/when this token was manually invalidated, for incident response or admin action.
  >
  > Soft delete pattern, atomic value.

### `api_audits`

[API Audit Trail] - Implements the requirement for comprehensive evidence logging and traceability of all API/omnichannel activity for compliance, security, forensics, and analytics. 

Business explanation: Stores each API request/event record, including actor, endpoint, action, decision logic, input/output hashes and outcomes. Strictly normalized: each row is atomic, no aggregates or summaries. Used to reconstruct incident timelines, regulatory reviews, or AI feedback for model retraining. For example, logging a PATCH to order status API or a failed webhook delivery. 

Key relationships: Linked to api_clients, api_tokens, and integration_channels (omnichannel source). 
Special behaviors: No deletion; retention policy and evidence archiving instead.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `api_client_id`
  > [API Client Reference] - Belonged API client from [api_clients.id](#api_clients).
  >
  > Source of the request/session/event.
- `api_token_id`
  > [API Token Reference] - Credential used for this operation, [api_tokens.id](#api_tokens).
  >
  > Enables evidence mapping, forensics, and access validation.
- `integration_channel_id`
  > [Integration Channel Reference] - Omnichannel source of request/event [integration_channels.id](#integration_channels).
  >
  > E.g., 'web', 'mobileapp', 'partner_erp'.
- `endpoint`
  > [API Endpoint Path] - Implements requirement for full request path traceability.
  >
  > Atomic path string, e.g. '/v2/order/{id}/update'.
- `http_method`
  > [HTTP Method] - Captures action type for compliance ('GET', 'POST', etc.).
  >
  > Atomic, not derived. Example: 'POST'.
- `actor_id`
  > [Actor/Subject ID] - UUID of user/service/entity causing action.
  >
  > Atomic reference. May reference user, partner, or system actor.
- `decision_log_id`
  > [AI Decision Log Reference] - If this API operation involved an automated/AI-based decision, reference unique log id.
  >
  > Supports explainability, model audit. May be nullable for non-AI flows.
- `request_hash`
  > [Request Body Hash] - Deterministic hash of input payload for integrity/evidence preservation.
  >
  > Prevents tampering. Atomic value, e.g. sha256(data).
- `response_hash`
  > [Response Body Hash] - Deterministic hash of returned payload for end-to-end evidence/auditing.
  >
  > Anti-tampering.
- `is_success`
  > [Success Flag] - Was this operation permitted/executed?
  >
  > For real-world forensics/audit, not derived. Atomic.
- `status_code`
  > [HTTP Status Code] - Final status from this request.
  >
  > Atomic integer. Example: 200, 401, 500.
- `created_at`
  > [Request Timestamp] - Time request was received and logged.
  >
  > Atomic timestamp for compliance and audit.

### `integration_channels`

[Integration Channel] - Implements the requirement to support omnichannel sources/connections and API gateways from the scalability and extensibility module. 

Business explanation: Each record represents an authorized source channel (e.g., web, mobile, external ERP, partner API gateway) that can initiate or receive events/integrations. Maintains 3NF and normalization: does not duplicate client/channel config, but links to associated sessions, audits, and webhooks. For example, a 'Point-of-Sale Kiosk' integration or a 'Partner CRM'. 

Key relationships: Referenced by channel_sessions, audits, and used for system events/analytics.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `channel_code`
  > [Channel Code] - Unique technical identifier for the source/integration channel.
  >
  > Required for business logic, routing, and automation. Example: 'mobileapp', 'partner_erp'.
- `channel_name`
  > [Channel Name] - Human readable, unique/channel-scoped label for easier management.
  >
  > Not a code/slug. Example: 'Main Web Storefront'.
- `is_active`
  > [Activation Status] - Indicates if the channel is currently enabled for communication and integrations.
  >
  > Atomic, not derived. For compliance and automation.
- `created_at`
  > [Registration Timestamp] - Channel setup/registration time for system auditability.
  >
  > Atomic timestamp. For evidence and analytics.
- `deleted_at`
  > [Deactivation (Soft Delete) Timestamp] - When this integration was formally ended (for audit/compliance).
  >
  > Implements soft delete pattern. Atomic timestamp.

### `channel_sessions`

[Channel Session/Instance] - Implements omnichannel session/lifecycle evidence for concurrent usage, device mapping, and scalability analysis, mapped to the requirement for cross-channel tracking and analytics. 

Business explanation: Each row represents a single connection period/session for a user/client/channel combination (e.g., a POS login, or mobile session). Restricts attributes to atomic values—expirations, tokens, associated references. For example, a customer on the web channel, switching to mobile with the same cart/order context.

Key relationships: Linked to integration_channels, api_tokens, and used for session state analytics.
Special behaviors: Session expiration/invalidations. All denormalized summaries go to mv_ tables only.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `integration_channel_id`
  > [Integration Channel Reference] - Channel for this session, [integration_channels.id](#integration_channels).
  >
  > Atomic; no duplicates.
- `api_token_id`
  > [API Token Reference] - Access token that initiated this session [api_tokens.id](#api_tokens).
  >
  > Atomic; session always requires a token.
- `user_id`
  > [User Reference] - Optional user UUID linked to this session.
  >
  > When present, identifies the direct user; otherwise, may be system/integration. Example: buyer channel login, or anonymous device.
- `session_key`
  > [Session Key] - System-generated, opaque identifier for this channel session instance.
  >
  > Atomic string, for referencing in logs or context-passing APIs.
- `started_at`
  > [Started At Timestamp] - When this channel session began.
  >
  > Exact audit evidence, for compliance and automation.
- `ended_at`
  > [Ended At Timestamp] - When session was terminated (timeout, logout).
  >
  > Not derived. Null if still open.

### `webhook_events`

[Webhook Event/Notification] - Implements the external/internal event delivery and audit requirements for extensible integration, system notification, and partner automation. 

Business explanation: Captures each system or API-originated webhook event, including delivery state and evidence for retries/audits. Fully normalized—relationship to originating channel, destination, and technical params only (payloads not stored here, only hashes/IDs). For example, a notification to a partner when an order is updated, or price changes via API. 

Key relationships: Linked to integration_channels. Used for compliance, analytics, and incident response.
Special behaviors: Delivery tracking, retry evidence, event outcome codification, no denormalization (all summaries are in mv_ tables only).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `integration_channel_id`
  > [Integration Channel Reference] - Channel that originated/scheduled the webhook [integration_channels.id](#integration_channels).
  >
  > Atomic for audit, routing, compliance.
- `event_type`
  > [Event Type] - Business/technical event code (e.g., 'order.updated', 'payment.completed').
  >
  > Atomic, not derived. For routing and compliance purposes.
- `destination_url`
  > [Destination URL] - Target endpoint for webhook delivery.
  >
  > Atomic and unique per webhook. Never duplicated. Example: 'https://partner.com/hook'.
- `attempt_count`
  > [Attempt Count] - Number of delivery attempts made to destination.
  >
  > Atomic for evidence/audit. For example, incremented on retry.
- `last_attempted_at`
  > [Last Attempted Timestamp] - When a delivery was last tried.
  >
  > Atomic value for audit/troubleshooting.
- `delivered_at`
  > [Delivery Success Timestamp] - When webhook was successfully delivered.
  >
  > Audit log reference. Null if not completed.
- `delivery_status`
  > [Latest Delivery Status] - Code indicating delivery result ('pending','success','failed').
  >
  > Atomic string, for system logic and evidence.
- `event_hash`
  > [Event Payload Hash] - Hashed identifier of request event, for evidence preservation and audit.
  >
  > Atomic and unique for event+payload. Example: sha256 of JSON/Payload.
